title: Agent Archivist authority-rotation record (archivist.control/v1)
description: The tenant-authority-signed record that chains one successor tenant-authority key to its predecessor (plan Section 5 control-plane boundary; the envelope's authority-chain rule, which this record type is the concrete form of). Stored at `tenants/<tenant>/v1/control/authority-rotations/<previous_key_id>.json`, where the key segment is the retiring authority key's ID under the pinned SHA-256 derivation, written only by the offline ControlAdminStore, read by every ingestion replica and verifying client that meets a control record or receipt certification signed by a key its pinned root does not directly name. The record retires one authority half and establishes the next: both public halves and both pinned-derivation key IDs ride in the signed bytes, so the chain a verifier walks is pure public material, exactly the property the receipt-key record gives the receipt chain (ID-009). Addressing is what makes the walk and the append-only history one design: the record sits at the predecessor's key ID, so the verifier holding the pinned root fetches the record that retires it, verifies the signature against the pinned half, trusts the successor the record establishes, and repeats — verification always starts at the pinned root and walks forward, never trusting a key because a record asserts it (the envelope's authority-chain rule). Successive authority rotations therefore append — one immutable object per retired key at that key's own address, an incompatible overwrite rejected outright — and no operation removes or rewrites a predecessor, so every chain link ever published stays in the store and keeps verifying. The predecessor signs: `authority_key_id` equals `previous_key_id` by construction, because the successor cannot be the witness to its own establishment — a rotation record signed by the key it establishes would be circular and verifies against nothing. The flat object is the complete record: the seven wrapper members every immutable control record carries (schemas/v1/control-envelope.json) plus the five chain members, closed with `additionalProperties: false` (docs/notes/control-trust-schemas.md). This immutable type carries no `authorization_epoch` — the envelope's write-class rule: an immutable record carries the epoch exactly when it is part of the record's identity, and this record's identity is the retired key ID its object key names, not an epoch; the authority chain has no epoch sequence, because the chain itself is the order — each link retires exactly the key the previous link established. Public material only, and doubly so (SEC-006, ID-001): the record carries both public halves and their derivable identifiers; the successor private half is generated by the tenant operator out of band and never appears in any record, file, or argument, and the predecessor private half retires with the rotation.

x-archivist.signature: control-record-v1 (schemas/v1/control-envelope.json): Ed25519 by the tenant authority named by `authority_key_id` over the RFC 8785 canonicalization of this object with the `authority_signature` member removed. The same construction, key namespace, and verifier core as every other control record; domain separation comes from `record_type`, so an authority rotation can never be replayed as another control record or the reverse. The signing key here is the predecessor — the still-current authority half at signing time — which is the chain rule itself: the record is the predecessor's signed witness to its own retirement, and the successor's half verifies only through it.
x-archivist.chainRule: The predecessor signs: `authority_key_id` equals `previous_key_id` (VAL-002 cross-field check, re-made by every verifier), and the record's Ed25519 signature verifies against `previous_public_key` — a rotation record signed by the successor key it establishes would be circular and is rejected, because verification never trusts a key because a record asserts it. The object key's segment equals `previous_key_id` in lowercase canonical hex (VAL-002, ID-008), so the record is addressable from exactly the material a verifier already trusts: holding pinned root R, the verifier fetches `authority-rotations/<R>.json`, checks the signature against R's half, and gains the successor named by `key_id` — then repeats from there until it reaches the signer named by the record it is actually verifying. The walk terminates at the pinned root because each link names its predecessor, and every link is immutable and retained, so a key's validity is computable from the store's public material alone: the half established by link L verifies from L's `signed_at` until the `signed_at` of the link whose `previous_key_id` names it — or indefinitely, if no such link exists. The chain has no epoch sequence: the links themselves are the order, each retiring exactly the key the previous link established.
x-archivist.overlapRule: The signing overlap is the envelope's named rotation-verification constant — `rotationVerificationOverlapHours` (24, plan Section 5: key rotation accepts old and new keys for 24 hours), the same constant the linked-client and rotation records pin, anchored here at this record's `signed_at`. From that instant, either authority half may sign control records and receipt-key certifications, and a verifier accepts either: the predecessor's signature through `previous_public_key` in this record, the successor's through the chain this record extends. The window bounds signing acceptance, never the validity of what was already signed: a control record or receipt certification the predecessor signed inside the window — its own `signed_at` at or before this record's `signed_at` plus the overlap — verifies for as long as the records are retained, and one the predecessor signed after the window fails closed, the plan Section 7.1 rule for security-bearing values. The overlap is tolerance for the boundary, never an extension of the predecessor's authority: the offline ControlAdminStore switches to the successor as its signing key at the rotation itself, and the window exists so administrative records and receipt certifications signed by the predecessor across the boundary — an in-flight batch, a certification racing the cutover — stay verifiable, and so every reader's view converges within its own 60-second trust cache rather than at the rotation instant.
x-archivist.replicaRule: An ingestion replica authenticating an uploader against a control record signed by an authority half its pinned root does not directly name resolves the signer through this chain, statelessly: the store's records are the only state (plan Section 3), and the 60-second trust cache bounds how long any earlier view is served (plan Section 5; EC-09) — the replica re-reads the chain like any other control record. Inside the overlap the replica accepts records signed by either half, each verified against its own establishing link; after the window a predecessor-signed record fails closed, and because acceptance is checked at the record's own `signed_at`, never at read time, records the predecessor legitimately signed before the window closed keep verifying forever. The offline ControlAdminStore writes this record signed by the predecessor and treats it as its own signing-key cutover: from the rotation instant it signs with the successor, inside the window a record it signed with either half verifies, and after the window a predecessor-signed write is rejected by every reader — the store gains nothing by signing with a retired half and the window costs no enforcement.
x-archivist.privateKey: both halves here are public — `previous_public_key` survives in this record precisely because verifiers need it to check this record's own signature and the window, and `public_key` is the half later records name in `authority_key_id`. No private material exists anywhere in this or any other record: the successor private half is generated by the tenant operator out of band, used to sign with, and reaches nothing else; the predecessor private half dies with the rotation (SEC-006). The gate's banned-name grammar plus the closed shape leave no member for material to ride in.
x-archivist.compatibility: member additions, redefinitions, and new required members are all v2 namespace events — the closed shape is the compatibility rule for control records (docs/notes/control-trust-schemas.md). The only in-place appends this schema tolerates are new tokens inside already-closed enums (record_type in the envelope; key_algorithm through the shared common definition), each shipped together with the readers that understand it

schema.description: The control trust namespace this record belongs to. Pinned by the shared definition; an unknown namespace fails closed before anything else is read.

record_type.description: This is an authority-rotation record. Narrowed from the envelope's closed record-type enum to a const of this schema's own token, so this file both names and is the type's complete contract.

record_kind.description: The authority-rotation record is an immutable record: written once at the predecessor-addressed key derived from its own identifiers, never overwritten — the store rejects an incompatible overwrite outright, so the only writer-visible repetition is a lost-response retry of identical bytes (the envelope's writeClasses rule). Immutability plus predecessor addressing is what makes the authority history append-only: each rotation is its own object at its own retired key's address, and there is no way to remove or rewrite a link — which is what lets a verifier re-walk the chain from the pinned root at any later time.

tenant_id.description: The tenant whose authority is rotating (plan Section 5). Must equal the tenant segment of the object key — the store derives the key from validated fields and refuses any mismatch (ID-008), and a reader can re-make the check, so a record served under another tenant's prefix is rejected as a cross-tenant forgery, not a naming oddity. The chain it establishes has no force outside this tenant.

previous_public_key.description: The retiring Ed25519 authority half — the key this rotation retires, and the half this record's own `authority_signature` verifies against. It survives here because a verifier meeting a record signed by this half needs the material to check both the signature and the overlap window, and no other control record retains a retired authority half: the chain walk arrives at this record carrying only key IDs, and the public half they resolve to is the one published in these signed bytes. Public material only (SEC-006).

previous_key_id.description: Identifier of the retiring authority key: the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of `previous_public_key` under the pinned derivation (VAL-002 cross-field derivation, re-made by every verifier — computable from this record's own `previous_public_key`). Identity member of the record: it equals the object key's segment in lowercase canonical hex, and it equals `authority_key_id` — the predecessor signs its own retirement, and a record whose signer differs from the key it retires is not a chain link. For the first link the value is the root the clients pinned during linking (ID-009), which is what lets the walk start there.

key_algorithm.description: Algorithm of both authority halves; Ed25519 only in v1. One member covers both keys deliberately — v1 has a single token, and the closed enum travels verified inside the predecessor-signed record, so neither half's algorithm is ever trusted from the record being verified. An unknown value fails closed before either key is used.

public_key.description: The successor Ed25519 authority half — the key this rotation establishes, which records signed after the cutover name in their `authority_key_id`. It verifies from the rotation's `signed_at` and never stops on its own; only a later link whose `previous_key_id` names it ends its validity. Public material only (SEC-006): the successor private half is generated by the tenant operator out of band and never appears in any record, file, or argument.

key_id.description: Identifier of the successor authority key: the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of `public_key` under the pinned derivation, computable from this record's own `public_key` (VAL-002). This is the value later control records and receipt-key certifications carry in `authority_key_id` once the cutover has happened — one key identity from this link to every record the successor signs.

signed_at.description: UTC time the predecessor authority signed this rotation, and the anchor of the signing-overlap window: for `rotationVerificationOverlapHours` (24, plan Section 5) from this instant either authority half may sign control records and receipt-key certifications and both verify — the envelope's named constant, pinned here and proven equal by the gate. It also bounds the predecessor's signing life: a record whose own `signed_at` falls after this instant plus the overlap and whose signer is the predecessor fails closed, while everything the predecessor signed before it keeps verifying for as long as the records are retained. Also audit evidence for when the operator cut the authority over; the chain is the logical order of the tenant's trust history, this is each link's wall-clock context.

authority_key_id.description: Identifier of the tenant authority key that signed this record: the retiring predecessor. Equals `previous_key_id` by the chain rule (VAL-002 cross-field check) — the successor cannot witness its own establishment, so the record is signed by the key it retires, and its signature verifies against `previous_public_key` in these same bytes. For the first link this is the root clients pinned during linking (ID-009); for later links it is the predecessor link's `key_id`.

authority_signature.description: The predecessor authority's Ed25519 signature under the control-record-v1 construction (schemas/v1/control-envelope.json): the RFC 8785 canonicalization of this object with this member removed, verified against `previous_public_key`. The one field the signer cannot cover, and the reason the retirement, both key identities, and the overlap's anchor are tamper-evident — a forged link would have to carry a signature the retired half never made, and a link signed by the successor instead verifies against nothing and is rejected.
